author_or_account: The Project on Workforce at Harvard
title: Pro-Worker AI: Expanding Human Capabilities with Collaborative Tools
published_window: 2026; four months before retrieval in the public search result
discussion_signal: The post translates the NBER framework into a public design argument: AI should expand human capability and the value of expertise, while new-task creation is distinguished from automation and expertise commodification. The visible discussion extends the question into implementation—whether employers can name the new work, preserve worker judgment, and make collaborative AI economically viable rather than merely cutting cost.
linked_research_question: When organizations describe AI as pro-worker, what observable new tasks, retained judgment, training, worker voice, pay, safety, and consumer outcomes distinguish capability expansion from disguised automation?
limits: Institutional post summarizes a conceptual paper rather than reporting new worker data
Visible comments are selected public reactions and not a representative worker sample
The discussion does not establish implementation, adoption, worker outcomes, or consumer benefit
